title: PostgreSQL Index Fundamentals
description: Understand database index anatomy, access methods, trade-offs between read acceleration and write overhead.

data.text: An **index** is an auxiliary data structure on disk that enables the PostgreSQL query engine to locate target rows in `O(log N)` time instead of performing a sequential table scan (`O(N)`). While indexes dramatically speed up read queries, each index incurs write overhead on every `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE`.

rows: Default for scalar values, primary keys, foreign keys, timestamps
Multi-key objects: JSONB, text search (tsvector), arrays
Geometric points, PostGIS geometries, range types (TSTZRANGE)
Massive append-only time-series tables physically clustered by date
Exact equality lookups on long string keys (WAL-logged since PG 10)

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: B-tree is the default index type in PostgreSQL.
Indexes trade read speed for write latency and disk storage.
Audit unused indexes using `pg_stat_user_indexes` to reclaim performance.
